'''Mysteries''' lists what the Star Wars CCG record does not yet know: results that sources disagree on, documents that were published but never preserved, and people and events that no surviving source explains. Each entry says what is known, with its sources, what is still open, and what would settle it. If you were there, kept the file, or have the photo, you can help answer it (see [[#How to help|How to help]]).

Each entry links to the article where the gap sits. The Talk page of that article usually has the full working notes.

== How to help ==
* '''Tell us what you remember.''' First-hand accounts are accepted sources on this wiki: Decipher kept few records, so a player's own account is cited as personal communication (see [[SWCCG Wiki:Style guide]]). Post on the article's Talk page, or on the Star Wars CCG forum or Slack, and say which entry you are answering.
* '''Send the document.''' Old slip-sheet PDFs, rules supplements, tournament packets, score sheets, newsletters, Squadron certificates and photos are all wanted. The file name and the date it was saved help identify it. A phone photo of a printed page is enough to start.
* '''Point to a source.''' A forum post, a DeckTech report, a magazine page or an archived web page that answers an entry is just as good.
* When an entry is answered, the article is updated with the source and the entry moves to [[#Solved|Solved]], with the answer and who supplied it.
* Editors can flag a gap where it sits in an article with <code><nowiki>{{Mystery|question=…|section=…}}</nowiki></code> ([[Template:Mystery]]); flagged articles are listed in [[:Category:Mysteries]].

== Events and results ==

=== Why did Brian Fred not play Day 2 of the 2000 World Championship? ===
[[Brian Fred]] won [[2000 Corellia Regionals]] on 3 June 2000 and is on Decipher's list of DecipherCon 2000 qualifiers.<ref name="dc00fin">[http://decipher.com/tournaments/deciphercon2000/swfinalists.html DecipherCon 2000: Star Wars CCG Qualifiers], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010308110320/http://decipher.com/tournaments/deciphercon2000/swfinalists.html Internet Archive]</ref> He has no row on Decipher's Day 2 results for the [[2000 Decipher World Championship]] at [[DecipherCon 2000]]. Three other named qualifiers are also missing from Day 2: [[Michael Riboulet]], [[Leszek Chrobak]] and [[Nick Reisch]]. [[Mike Kessling]] filled Riboulet's chair; who took the other chairs is only an editorial reading.<ref name="t2000w">[[Talk:2000 Decipher World Championship]], Qualifiers notes (October 2026).</ref>
* '''Open:''' Did Brian Fred travel to Kissimmee? Did he decline or pass on his invitation, and who played in his place? The same questions apply to Chrobak and Reisch.
* '''What would settle it:''' an account from Brian Fred or another 2000 finalist, a 2000 DeckTech or forum post, or Decipher's alternates list.

=== Who won the 2000 Toola Regionals? ===
Decipher's 2000 Regionals listing names Bert-Olof Lundin as the [[2000 Toola Regionals]] qualifier. The DecipherCon 2000 qualifier list and the Day 2 standings name [[Jesper Larsson]], and Martin Akesson wrote that Larsson won the Toola final.<ref name="dc00fin" /><ref name="t2000w" /> The article shows both.<ref>[[Talk:2000 Toola Regionals]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>
* '''What would settle it:''' a Toola 1999–2000 results sheet, or an account from either player.

=== 1997 qualifiers: Atlanta, Mobile, Denver and Origins ===
Decipher's 1997 qualifier list<ref name="q97">[http://search.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/regionalsandopens.html 1997 World Finals: Regionals and Opens], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990503132332/http://search.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/regionalsandopens.html Internet Archive]</ref> and the NewsFlash event reports disagree on several winners:<ref name="t97">[[Talk:1997 Decipher World Championship]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>
* '''Dagobah (Atlanta and Mobile):''' the list gives Atlanta (Dragon Con, 29 June) to Chris Vickers and Mobile (MobiCon, 30 May) to Shelby Abercrombie; the NewsFlash report says Vickers won Mobile, beating Stephen Lanza. The list may have the two swapped, which leaves the winner of [[1997 Dagobah Regionals (Atlanta)]] open.
* '''Denver (31 May):''' the list names Thaddeus Chenoweth; the NewsFlash report says Joshua Andersen beat Chenoweth 2–0 in the final.
* '''Origins Open (18 July):''' Decipher lists Rick Sollman as champion; a fan compilation on the forum gives Clint Hays 1st and T.J. Holman 2nd.
* '''Sullust (Milan):''' the list dates it 13 September 1997; the Deck Designs label reads "10/97" ([[1997 Sullust Regionals]]).

=== Early World Championship fields and standings ===
* '''[[1996 Decipher World Championship]]:''' InQuest counts 38 players; 35 regional winners plus Mikaelian make 36 named. Who were the other two?<ref>[[Talk:1996 Decipher World Championship]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>
* '''[[1997 Decipher World Championship]]:''' the field is given as 52 (Wikipedia), about 64 (Eric Berger's 2015 recollection) or 53 (51 qualifiers and 2 invitees). The players' statement pages were never archived.<ref name="t97" /><ref>[[Talk:1997 Decipher World Championship First Anthology Sealed]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>
* '''[[1998 Decipher World Championship]]:''' places 5–12 on Sunday are not named beyond Trandosite's twelve, and the Sunday sealed winner is not on the packet.<ref>[[Talk:1998 Decipher World Championship]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>
* '''[[1999 Decipher World Championship]]:''' no player packet for 1999 has been found, and Day 1 places outside the final twelve are not on an official sheet.<ref>[[Talk:1999 Decipher World Championship]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>
* '''[[2002 World Championship]]:''' no full Day 2 Swiss standings and no Top 8 pairings were published; winners of the Players Committee side events at [[DecipherCon 2002]] are unknown.<ref>[[Talk:DecipherCon 2002]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>

=== DecipherCon 1999 side events ===
[[DecipherCon 1999 Progressive Sealed Deck]] survives as two differing score sheets (34 and 68 players) with no winner; Martin Akesson wrote that he won it against [[Aldrin Long]]. The winners of the Allegiances and Star Wars Iron Man events are also unknown, and it is not known whether a two-game sheet belongs to [[DecipherCon 1999 Iron Man]] or to a separate event.<ref>[[Talk:DecipherCon 1999]], Possibly faulty data.</ref> The fourth member of the winning [[DecipherCon 1999 Team Event]] team is also in question: Akesson's 2000 interview names Akesson, [[Paul Todd Feldman|Paul Feldman]], [[Koen Meijssen]] and [[Yannick Lapointe]], while Feldman's 2025 recollection names others.<ref>[[Talk:DecipherCon 1999 Team Event]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>

=== FreedomCon and the 2001 World Championship ===
DeckTech's FreedomCon page gives [[Hayes Hunter]] 3rd and Brian Hunter 4th; a 2020 forum post recalls them the other way round. Places 5–8 are known only from forum recollections, with no bracket or report.<ref>[[Talk:2001 Decipher World Championship]], Possibly faulty data.</ref><ref name="tfc">[[Talk:FreedomCon]], Possibly faulty data.</ref> The card pool actually used at [[FreedomCon]] is not confirmed from a FreedomCon source, and no winner has been found for the FreedomCon Philadelphia 2002 Star Wars CCG event.<ref name="tfc" />

=== Tournaments with no recorded winner or standings ===
* [[2000 Boston Grand Slam]] (winner printed "?") and twelve later Grand Slam 2000 weekends (Linköping, Houston, Landshut, Virginia Beach, Brussels, Nashville, Los Angeles, Blue Springs, Krakow, Birmingham, Minneapolis and Phoenix). Nothing found so far shows that they were held as scheduled. [[2000 Seattle Grand Slam]] is dated January by Decipher's calendar and February by its Deck Designs label.<ref>[[Talk:2000 Seattle Grand Slam]], Possibly faulty data and Missing data.</ref>
* [[2002 Dagobah Regionals]]: only the announcement has been found; it is not known whether it was held.<ref>[[Talk:2002 Dagobah Regionals]], Missing data.</ref>
* [[2013 Texas Mini Worlds]] and [[2013 Alderaan Regionals]]: the surviving decklist PDFs do not name a champion.<ref>[[Talk:2013 Texas Mini Worlds]] and [[Talk:2013 Alderaan Regionals]].</ref> At the [[2013 World Championship]], [[Justin Desai]] beat [[Reid Smith]] in the final, but the order of the other Day 3 players (3rd to 8th) has not been found, only seven of the eight Day 3 players are known, and [[Matthew Harrison-Trainor]]'s Day 2 decks differ between the Day 2 table and the Day 3 PDF.<ref>[[Talk:2013 World Championship]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>
* [[2014 US Nationals]]: the event site is not known.<ref>[[Talk:2014 US Nationals]].</ref>
* [[2014 European Championship]]: the site is not known, and no decklist PDF or typed list for the main event is on the Players Committee's decklists page.<ref>[[Talk:2014 European Championship]], Missing data.</ref>
* [[1996 GenCon Open]]: InQuest names [[Michael Mikaelian]] as the winner over [[Joe Alread]], but the month, field size and format are not known.<ref>[[Talk:1996 GenCon Open]], Missing data.</ref>
* [[2026 Retro World Championship]]: the Players Committee posted four players' lists, but no event page; the day, the number of players, the standings and the winner are not known.<ref>[[Talk:2026 Retro World Championship]], Missing data.</ref> The Tatooine event of the [[2026 Regional Championships]] (Ken Cross, Mark Billings, Paul Coggins, Randy Scott) has no known date, site, attendance or winner.<ref>[[Talk:2026 Regional Championships]].</ref>
* Online events: some match winners are not named in the results posts of the [[2019 Outrider Cup]] and the [[2021 Outrider Cup]] (game 8, Harrison-Trainor against Fürgut); the [[2025 Retro Invitational Player's Ball]] final, semifinal and quarterfinal results were not posted; [[2026 Retro League Event 1]] has no standings below 10th and its Prelude no winner; [[2023 Beezer Bowl]] has no full standings.<ref>[[Talk:2019 Outrider Cup]], [[Talk:2021 Outrider Cup]], [[Talk:2025 Retro Invitational Player's Ball]], [[Talk:2026 Retro League Event 1]] and [[Talk:2023 Beezer Bowl]], Missing data.</ref>

=== Score sheets, decks and listings that were not preserved ===
* '''[[DecipherCon 1999]] side events:''' no score sheet survives for the Thursday and Friday heats of [[DecipherCon 1999 Players Choice]], the Saturday heat of [[DecipherCon 1999 No Such Thing As Luck]], the Sunday heats of [[DecipherCon 1999 Allegiances]] and [[DecipherCon 1999 Japanese Sealed Deck]], or [[DecipherCon 1999 EPP Overdrive]]. The rules of the "Enhanced Sealed Deck (ECC+EPP)" event ([[Enhanced Format Sealed Deck]]) and Decipher's own descriptions of [[Allegiances: Multi-Deck Format]] and [[Players' Choice Sealed Deck]] are not preserved either.
* '''1996 and 2000 qualifier listings:''' Decipher's 1996 list gives no date for Ralltiir A (Essen) and no field sizes ([[1996 Decipher World Championship]]). No 2000 Regionals listing was captured for Calamari, Chandrila, Ithor or Outer Rim, so their dates and sites are unknown ([[2000 Decipher World Championship]]).<ref name="t2000w" />
* '''[[1997 Decipher World Championship First Anthology Sealed]]:''' no rules sheet for the event has been found, so its deck size and game length are unknown.
* '''Mark Latham's UK decks:''' his results page names decks that were not preserved: the Light decks of [[1998 Loughborough Regional Qualifier]] (lst4) and [[January 1999 Birmingham tournament]] (lst8), and the Dark decks of [[1999 Bisley RP tournament]] (dst11) and [[August 1999 Taunton tournament]] (dst12). See also [[Trandosite decks]].
* '''[[2004 World Championship]]:''' Day 3 places are not known for [[Nick Jones]] (1st after Day 2) and [[Lee Edwards]].
* '''[[2006 World Championship]]:''' [[Nate Meeker]]'s Day 3 Dark deck "Scum Solid" was posted on DeckTech, but that list was not archived.
* '''[[2011 World Championship]]:''' no Day 1 decklist PDF is available, so [[2011 Worlds Day 2 Josh Mack DS Same As Day 1|Josh Mack's Day 1 Dark deck]] is not known.
* '''[[2013 Alderaan Regionals]]:''' [[Chris Menzel]]'s typed sheets are headed "California 2013" and dated 13 July 2013, though they are bound with the Alderaan sheets. Which event were they for?
* '''[[2014 Match Play Championship]]:''' neither of Chris Wirfs' consolation sheets marks Light or Dark, so which scan is which is not known ([[2014 Match Play Championship Consolation Chris Wirfs LS It Is The Future You See (V)]]).
* '''[[2022 Match Play Championship]]:''' the full Top 8 order needs a source (the Players Committee event page).<ref>[[Talk:2022 Match Play Championship]].</ref>
* '''[[2022 Retro League Event 5]]:''' the points worked out from the posted results do not follow the posted standings order (for example Andrew Bethell's 24 is two more than a 6–0 winner should earn).<ref>[[Talk:2022 Retro League Event 5]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>
* '''[[2026 State Championships]]:''' the standings image of the Maryland event (Gambrills, 2026) is not preserved in the archive.
* '''Decklists not published:''' Day 1, Day 3 and team decklists of the [[2012 World Championship]] (only Day 2 was posted); [[Joe Giannetti]]'s Day 2 Dark deck at the [[2015 World Championship]].<ref>[[Talk:2012 World Championship]] and [[Talk:2015 World Championship]], Missing data.</ref>
* '''Decklists with a card or start missing:''' as posted, [[2022 EGP Matt Wadden LS Qui Communing]], [[2015 MPC Tom Hollingworth DS Endor Operations]], [[2017 European Championship Day 2 Mike Rosenberger DS Mains]] and [[2026 Retro Worlds Jeremy Christoffel LS Echo Base Operations]] have 59 cards; [[2018 European Championship Day 2 Alex T. DS Mains]] gives no starting location. Some lines on [[2007 Worlds Day 2 Lee Edwards LS Plead My Case To The Senate]] and [[2007 Worlds Day 2 Lee Edwards DS Drop]] cannot be read.

=== Unidentified players ===
Some decklist sheets have a blank or unreadable Name box; they are listed on [[Unknown players]]. Players known only by a handle include [[Domestique]] and [[AceMace]] (last name).
* '''Final Confrontation, [[2000 Decipher World Championship]]:''' the seated long-haired person at the head of the table in the Final Confrontation video is not identified; it is not [[Justin Pakes]], and the standing ponytail in the same frames is [[Joe Helfrich]].<ref>[[Talk:Justin Pakes]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>
* '''Portland, [[2000 Seattle Grand Slam|Grand Slam 2000]]:''' the Portland winner "Joe Olson" is not clearly the modern [[Joe Olson]] (arebelspy).<ref>[[Talk:2000 Seattle Grand Slam]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>
* '''Known by part of a name:''' [[Alex T.]] (surname not published), "Marcus" in row 26 of the [[2026 European Championship]] Day 1, jwesselss at the [[2025 Scavenger Superbowl Showcase]], [[Darth Grader]] (Mark; surname), [[JP Peltier]] (what "JP" stands for), and the guests GEMP Tom, MHT and Ideatrack on [[Corran on the Horn]].
* '''A tournament hall in ''[[One With The Force]]'':''' the teaser's hall shot (0:47) has a DGMA banner, but the event is not identified.<ref>[[Talk:One With The Force]], Missing data.</ref>

== People and Squadron Members ==

=== Squadron Members outside the published lists ===
The [[Squadron Members]] roster is built from a fan tribute page that called itself complete and from decipher.com's region listings of 1999–2001.<ref name="fan-roster">[https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/SMs.html Squadron Members], Corellian Engineering Corporation fan site. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009142705/https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/SMs.html Internet Archive]</ref> [[Scott Lingrell]] says the list is not complete: "Also, it's not complete. I was gold 60 I think. Rogue 60 sorry".<ref name="slack-lingrell-2026">Star Wars CCG Slack, #swccgdiscussion, Scott Lingrell, 9 October 2026.</ref> The fan Rogue table ends at Rogue 40 ([[Doug Faust]]).<ref>[[Talk:Squadron Members]].</ref>
* '''Open:''' Who held Rogue 41 and up, and other callsigns missing from the fan table? Who served before 1999, when decipher.com did not yet list members by region?
* '''Vacant slots:''' both surviving rosters leave Gold 10, 21–23, 25–26 and 99–100, Red 9, 28–29, 75–76 and 120, and Bravo 22 empty. Were they unfilled, or are the holders missing?<ref name="tsm">[[Talk:Squadron Members]].</ref>
* '''Callsigns that disagree:''' the archived decipher.com region listings and the fan table give different callsigns for [[Alisa LaPorte]] (Gold 52 or Gold 51), [[Mike Ryan]] (Gold 50 or Gold 54) and [[Mike Burgess]] (Red 107 or Red 108). About thirty-five other members have a different hometown in the two sources; each difference is noted on the member's Talk page.<ref>[[Talk:Alisa LaPorte]], [[Talk:Mike Ryan]] and [[Talk:Mike Burgess]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>
* '''What would settle it:''' Squadron newsletters, e-mails, certificates or ID cards, and accounts from former Squadron Members and Squadron Leaders.

=== Decipher staff known only from the anagram list ===
The fan anagram list names [[Becky Higgerson]], [[Leslie Burns]], [[Keith Skipton]], [[Mike Gray]], [[Bob Madison]] and [[Jason Winter]] as Decipher staff, but nothing found so far gives their role or dates (see [[Anagramed Decipherians]]). It is also unconfirmed whether [[Sean Smallman]] and the "Shawn Smallman" of the [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] credits are the same person.
* '''[[Bob Madison]] or [[Will Madison]]?''' The two-player rules booklet lists both as playtesters; the fan anagram list gives "[Bob/Will] Madison" for [[Imperial Trooper Guard Dainsom]] without saying which one.<ref>[[Talk:Bob Madison]] and [[Talk:Will Madison]].</ref>
* '''[[Mike Gray]]:''' the booklet thanks "Mike Gray and Carol Wisely"; he may be the Parker Brothers and Hasbro designer Michael Gray, but nothing found so far confirms it.<ref>[[Talk:Mike Gray]], Possibly faulty data.</ref> [[Jim Van Fleet]]'s Decipher service is also uncited.
* '''[[Richard Borg]]:''' Days of Wonder lists ''Star Wars: The CCG'' among his designs, while the booklet only thanks him "for rogue design in an elegant system". It is also not known whether the playtester Sandy Borg is related.<ref>[[Talk:Richard Borg]].</ref>

=== Other people questions ===
* [[Nick Reisch]] and [[Nathan Reisch]]: one person or two?<ref name="t2000w" />
* [[James Monsebroten]]: no record has been found of him playing Star Wars CCG at the 1999 or 2000 World Championship, and Decipher gave him three hometowns (Coquitlam, Burnaby and Kamloops).<ref>[[Talk:James Monsebroten]].</ref>
* [[Gregory Reid]]: Martin Akesson called him a 1996 and 1997 finalist; the packets that would confirm it have not been found.<ref>[[Talk:1999 Decipher World Championship]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>
* [[Jim Colson]]: dates of his tournament director and Star Trek CCG Ambassador work, and whether he appears in Radio Free Decipher broadcast 10.<ref>[[Talk:Jim Colson]].</ref>
* [[Joseph Wisniewski]]: does the forum account geraldkw belong to him?<ref>[[Talk:Joseph Wisniewski]].</ref> [[Francis Lalumiere]]: the dates of his writing for Decipher.<ref>[[Talk:Francis Lalumiere]].</ref>
* [[Jared Napolitano]]: when his Retro League assistance ended (2024, or did he still handle prizes in 2025?).<ref>[[Talk:Jared Napolitano]].</ref>
* [[Brianna Emery]] and [[James Emery]]: Decipher's DecipherCon 1999 photos are the only record; was Brianna a player, a volunteer or Decipher staff?<ref>[[Talk:Brianna Emery]] and [[Talk:James Emery]], Missing data.</ref>
* [[Ben Lacey]]: is the 1999 Star Trek finalist Ray Lacey the other member of Decipher's "Lacey gang"? Did Ben play Star Wars CCG?<ref>[[Talk:Ben Lacey]], Missing data.</ref> [[Kim Burns]]: is she the "Kim Burns of Michigan" on Radio Free Decipher broadcast 10?<ref>[[Talk:Kim Burns]].</ref>
* Decipher staff whose dates or roles are still open: [[Monica Jones]] (marketing titles, and whether she succeeded [[Carol Wisely]]), [[Tom Lischke]] (employment dates), [[Evan Lorentz]] (start date), [[Sandy Wible]] (dates as Rebel Base Leader), [[Kendrick Summers]] (host of Radio Free Decipher broadcast 2, uncited). [[Stacy Mollema]]'s Lucasfilm licensing role and the playtesting of [[Curtiss Murphy]] and [[Mark Schaffer]] rest on single sources.<ref>The Talk page of each person, Missing data.</ref>
* "Ross": [[Jerry Darcy]] on Radio Free Decipher 14 says the early team was "just Tom and me and Warren, and Dan and Ross"; Ross is not identified ([[Creators of SWCCG]]).<ref>[[Talk:Creators of SWCCG]], Missing data.</ref>

== Virtual cards and slip sheets ==

=== Lost original slip sheets ===
The Players Committee replaced several Virtual sets' release sheets with later revisions, and some first releases were never archived:
* '''[[Virtual Set 6: City In The Clouds]]''': the first release of 21 November 2003 is not preserved. The 31 December 2003 interim rules supplement ([https://web.archive.org/web/20040615005231/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Resources/v6changes.pdf v6changes.pdf], ten cards, "not final") and the sheets of 12 January and 12 October 2004 survive.
* '''[[Virtual Set 9: Sanctuary Moon]]''', '''[[Virtual Set 10: Fourth Anthology]]''' and '''[[Virtual Set 11: Gathering Storm]]''': the PC's Virtual Cards page listed "Virtual Set 9 Final.pdf" and "Virtual Set 10.pdf" ([https://web.archive.org/web/20050829203847/http://www.swccgpc.com/virtualcards.htm 29 August 2005]), then VirtualSet9.pdf, VirtualSet10.pdf and VirtualSet11GoldEdition.pdf ([https://web.archive.org/web/20060206230426/http://www.swccgpc.com/virtualcards.htm 6 February 2006]). None of those files was captured; the surviving copies are the later Remaster files.
* '''Virtual Set 11 Remaster''': the December 2006 issue is lost; the surviving file is the 25 June 2007 re-edit.
* '''[[Virtual Set 12: Martyrs & Magistrates]]''': the download library says "Added on: 22-Aug-2006", but the earliest surviving sheet is dated 9 January 2007.
* '''What would settle it:''' any of those PDFs from an old hard drive, CD or e-mail, or the printed slips.

=== Release dates not found ===
No release or tournament-legal post survives for Virtual Sets 9 to 17 (see each set's Talk page, for example [[Talk:Virtual Set 9: Sanctuary Moon]]). The exact day of the first [[Virtual Shields]] PDF and of Virtual Set 8.1 (May 2012, [[Virtual Block 8]]) are also unknown, as is whether a VirtualCards18.pdf ever existed ([[2009 Virtual Block Reorganization]]).
* '''Legal dates:''' [[Virtual Set 1: Legacy|Virtual Set 1]] is dated 9 March 2002, but decks filed under [[Premiere - Original VS1]] have legal days from 8 February 2002. Nothing found so far gives the legal day of [[Premiere - Virtual Block 8.2]], of the four 8.2 preview cards ([[Premiere - Virtual Block 8.1]]), or of the "V9.1 Preview Set" of 9 July 2013 ([[Premiere - Virtual Block 8.3]]). The 10 January 2014 release of [[Republic At War (Virtual Block 9)|Virtual Block 9.1]] has no citation.
* '''Announcements:''' the 2009 Block reorganization was announced in August or September 2009, but the first firm date is the 7 December 2009 PDF stamp ([[Talk:Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]]). The [[2014 Virtual Card Pool Reset]] announcement is dated 25 July 2014 by the Players Committee byline and 14 July by Category One Games. Whether the Players Committee ever formally renamed Standard to [[Open]] is not known.
* '''Counts:''' the [[Republic At War (Virtual Block 9)]] cover counts 77 cards, while its card list has 75 rows. [[Reflections Gold]]: the Collecting Encyclopedia lists a standalone Trade Federation Tactics, while the forum set list has the combo card.
* '''More dates:''' no dated launch sheet survives for [[Virtual Set 5: A Dark Time|Virtual Set 5]] (the file's PDF date is 11 June 2003). For [[Virtual Set 13: Remote Outpost|Virtual Set 13]] and [[Virtual Set 16: Revenge Of The Sith|Virtual Set 16]] only the sheet dates are known. Which sheet first printed the 28 [[Virtual Shields]] that are not on a Block release sheet is not known.
* '''[[Cancelled Virtual Sets]]:''' no Players Committee source describes the plan for or the cancellation of [[Virtual Set 19: Galaxy At War]], and the fate of the World Championship "mini, 12 card set" against the "9.2" listing is not settled.<ref>[[Talk:Cancelled Virtual Sets]], Missing data.</ref>

=== First printings that were not preserved ===
* The first Legacy printings of Virtual Blocks 1 to 5 (September 2009) were not archived; the surviving sheets were re-made later ([[PC Legacy Virtual Transcription Error History]]). Each errata article that starts from them says so, for example [[Away Put Your Weapon (V) (Errata)]] and [[Careful Planning (V) (Virtual Block 4) (Errata)]]. The first Virtual Block 7 printing is also lost ([[Restore Freedom To The Galaxy (Virtual Block 7) (Errata 2)]], [[Vader's Mask (Errata)]]).
* The December 2006 wordings of [[Tusken Breath Mask (V) (Virtual Set 8)]] and [[I'm With You Too (V) (Virtual Set 9: Sanctuary Moon)]] before their errata of 17 September 2007 are not preserved, and the text of [[I Wonder Who They Found (V) (Virtual Set 9)]] before its errata is unknown.

=== Errata dated only by "by" ===
Many Players Committee errata to Virtual Block cards are dated only by the first surviving copy that shows the new text, for example the PC website card lists "by 21 July 2012" or the PC card images "by 25 February 2013"; the real errata date is earlier and unknown.<ref>[http://www.starwarsccg.org/cardlists/VBlock1Name.html Virtual Block 1 card list], Players Committee (card texts in the icon tooltips). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20121213050628/http://www.starwarsccg.org:80/cardlists/VBlock1Name.html Internet Archive, 13 December 2012]</ref> Example: [[Deep Hatred (V) (Errata)]]. The wording of [[Field Dressing (Errata 2)|Field Dressing]] before "and, if 'hit,' is restored to normal" is also unknown.
* '''Errata whose exact words are not known:''' [[Scoundrel's Luck (Errata)]], [[Imperial Navigation Charts (Errata)]] and [[Kessel Surveillance System (Errata)]] (the sheet's own words), [[AT-RT (Errata 3)]], [[Coruscant: Main Power Plant (Errata)]] (the earlier wording), and a middle version of [[In The Hands Of The ISB (Errata)|In The Hands Of The ISB]] whose forum post was not archived.
* '''Errata dates:''' the date of the Players Committee change to [[Blast The Door, Kid!]] is known only to lie between two sheets. For [[Garindan (V)]], [[Grievous, Hunter Of Jedi]], [[IG-100 MagnaGuard]] and [[A Stunning Move / A Valuable Hostage (V) (Virtual Block 7) (Errata)|A Stunning Move]], the master list's April 2013 cover and its 2014 page footers leave the effective date of the full text unknown.
* '''Texts with no dated source:''' the Players Committee card data and website card list carry wordings that no dated sheet has: a whole-card rewrite of [[Fleet Security Protocols]] (was it real errata?), a third wording of [[Luke's Blaster Pistol (V) (Virtual Block 2)]], and a different trigger on [[Kessel Surveillance System (Errata 5)|Kessel Surveillance System]].

=== Card images and early texts ===
* [[Slip Sliding Away (V)]] had no Holotable image when it was released.
* Older card images print a different destiny or uniqueness from the slip, with no dated change: for example [[Ke Chu Ke Kukuta? (V)]] (uniqueness bullet on the Block 3 caption only) and [[Another Pathetic Lifeform (Coruscant) (V)]] (destiny 5 on the image, 0 on the slip).<ref>[[Talk:Ke Chu Ke Kukuta? (V)]] and [[Talk:Another Pathetic Lifeform (Coruscant) (V)]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>
* [[Tragedy Of Plagueis]]: a same-day image replacement (an icon change) is not explained.
* The earliest texts of the Set 0 shields (2014) and of [[Planetary Defenses (V)]] (2015) are unknown: the PC's Holotable image history starts on 8 July 2018.<ref>[https://github.com/swccgpc/holotable/commit/022435b7929e4de26dafbcb1de2ec1d6d04d2153 swccgpc/holotable, first commit of the Virtual card images, 8 July 2018] (GitHub; preserved copy pending).</ref>

== Rules documents ==
These official rules documents are named in Decipher's or the Players Committee's indexes but no copy has been found:<ref>[https://github.com/billbisco/ai-team-skills/blob/main/shared/swccg-rules/SOURCES.md SOURCES.md, Gaps] (ai-team-skills); Decipher rules and FAQ indexes, [https://web.archive.org/web/19970607094415/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/index.html 7 June 1997], [https://web.archive.org/web/19980213113323/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/index.html 13 February 1998], [https://web.archive.org/web/19990504152957/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/index.html 4 May 1999]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20100714225208/http://starwarsccg.org:80/index.php?option=com_phocadownload&view=sections&Itemid=63 PC downloads, 14 July 2010].</ref>
* Premiere rules text file on Decipher's FTP site (swrules.txt)
* First Anthology rules supplement sheet (May 1997)
* Official Tournament Sealed Deck rules supplement
* FAQ, first partial preliminary release (5 June 1997, faq060597.pdf)
* Current Rulings of 2 December 1997, 12 February 1998, 20 May 1998 and 29 March 1999
* Glossary 1.x, if it existed, and the monthly Glossary Supplement versions between 30 May 2001 and 29 January 2002
* Players Committee "Advanced Rulebook Update – June, 2010"
See [[Rules]].

== Players Committee and Decipher history ==
=== Designing the game ===
The designers' own accounts disagree on several points (see [[Design of Star Wars CCG]]):
* Who first proposed Force drains: [[Chuck Kallenbach]] credits playtester [[Mark Tuttle]]; [[Jerry Darcy]] says several people reached the idea.
* Darcy's first day (14 April or 1 April 1995) and his last set (''Endor'' or ''Death Star II''); whether he was at the review that strengthened the operatives.
* Whether work on ''Star Wars'' began right after the ''Star Trek'' launch ([[Tom Braunlich]], 2022) or about a year later ([[Rollie Tesh]], 1999); who first wanted "a random element like dice" for destiny.
* When Mark Tuttle started playtesting: ''A New Hope'' (2018 interview) or Premiere (WARS Radio, 2004).<ref>[[Talk:Mark Tuttle]], Possibly faulty data.</ref>
* The design firm's name: "Technical Design Services" or "Technical Game Services" ([[Inspirations for Star Wars CCG]]).
* Which cuts of the fonts Decipher used (Berthold's BQ releases or the earlier BE), whether its title face was Fiorello or a look-alike, and which faces the Japanese and other foreign-language printings used ([[Typography of Star Wars CCG cards]]).

=== Products and the company ===
* '''[[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]]:''' [[Jim Colson]] says mass-market boxes held white-border packs and hobby boxes black-border packs; the Collecting Encyclopedia says Limited packs went in the first ~50,000 boxes and Unlimited after.
* '''[[The Empire Strikes Back Introductory Two-Player Game]]:''' the exclusives are Common (Decipher) or Premium (Collecting Encyclopedia); the Light Side Restraining Bolt's copyright year (1995 or 1996).
* '''[[SWCCG Memorabilia]]:''' the Executive Gift Set is dated 2001 by the Collecting Encyclopedia, while Andy Talaga and Matt Manning place the first copies at a 1997 or 1998 Christmas party; how many were made (about 250, or more). The 1999 Finalist shirt count ("approximately 120").
* '''[[Decipher]]:''' the embezzlement figures (more than US$1.5 million plea, about US$8.9 million settlement, about US$9 million losses); the 2005 layoffs (up to 40, or more than 90; [[Decipher after the Star Wars license]]); whether Decipher sold its remaining stock to a wholesaler in 2001 ([[Unofficial repackaged products]]).
* '''[[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]]:''' the actual ship date of ''Scum and Villainy'' (announced for 11 July 2001).
* '''[[GEMP]]:''' when Star Wars CCG GEMP first ran on a Players Committee host (a gemp.starwarsccg.org capture exists from January 2019; the move is dated September 2020).
* '''[[Playtest cards]]:''' nothing found so far says when or where Decipher showed its cards to Lucasfilm, how many were made, or when the earliest batch was printed; Brian Kallenbach's own post of the batch has not been found.<ref>[[Talk:Playtest cards]], Missing data.</ref>
* '''Undated releases:''' the month of the [[Premiere starter deck rulebook]] (the booklet prints only © 1995); the exact day [[Holotable]] launched in 2004; the 19 July 2000 release of [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]] is uncited; the October 1998 start of [[Trandosite]] is uncited; the date of the Bainbridge Island meeting with [[Richard Garfield]].<ref>Talk pages of [[Talk:Premiere starter deck rulebook|Premiere starter deck rulebook]], [[Talk:Holotable|Holotable]], [[Talk:Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]], [[Talk:Trandosite|Trandosite]] and [[Talk:Richard Garfield|Richard Garfield]], Missing data.</ref>

=== Players Committee and Decipher records ===
* The date and story of the starwarsccg.org takeover are not known as a full narrative ([[History of the Players Committee]]).
* DecipherCon 2000 sound bytes and video clips, Decipher's FTP files and many single-photo pages were never archived (see [[Talk:DecipherCon website]] and [[Talk:Decipher.com]]).
* The 80 kb stream of the DecipherCon 2000 Star Wars CCG finals is lost; only the 20 kb stream survives ([[Talk:Decipher.com downloads]]). The Jabba's Palace installers on Decipher's FTP site are not known to survive ([[Talk:Ftp.decipher.com]]).

== Solved ==
* '''What did "FL" mean on Squadron slots?''' Flight Leader, a key volunteer who worked more directly with Decipher. Answered by Ming Huo and Scott Lingrell on the Star Wars CCG Slack, 9 October 2026 (see [[Squadron Members]]).<ref name="slack-lingrell-2026" /> The answer was added to the Talk pages of the 198 Squadron Members whose notes still called the meaning unknown or listed it as missing data (13 November 2026).
